operation_logs.configuration_details: Changed the edge gateway upstream for the orders route from orders-v1:8443 to orders-v2:8443.
operation_logs.raw_evidence: Approved change record: orders route upstream set to orders-v2:8443; prior value orders-v1:8443.

operation_logs.configuration_details: Applied the updated orders upstream configuration to both edge gateway nodes.
operation_logs.raw_evidence: Deployment completed on edge-gw-03 and edge-gw-04; configuration checksum matched the approved change.

operation_logs.configuration_details: Orders traffic was routed to the newly configured upstream.
operation_logs.incident_symptoms: Orders requests returned HTTP 503 from both gateway nodes.
operation_logs.raw_evidence: Gateway log: upstream connect error for orders-v2:8443; connection refused. The first 503 alert followed DEP-7421 by three minutes.

operation_logs.configuration_details: Restored the orders upstream to orders-v1:8443 on both edge gateway nodes.
operation_logs.incident_symptoms: HTTP 503 responses stopped after the prior upstream was restored.
operation_logs.raw_evidence: Post-rollback gateway logs show successful connections to orders-v1:8443; the 503 alert cleared at 09:23Z.

diagnosis_summary: The deployment applied a changed orders upstream that refused gateway connections, producing HTTP 503 responses on both edge nodes. Restoring the prior upstream cleared the alert, strongly linking the change to the incident.
alternative_causes: A separate orders-v2 service outage could also produce connection refusals, but the logs show that restoring the previous upstream cleared the gateway errors.

causal_evidence_chain.evidence_summary: The change record identifies the upstream switch from orders-v1:8443 to orders-v2:8443.
The deployment applied that upstream configuration to both affected gateway nodes.
Shortly after deployment, both gateways returned 503 responses and logged connection refusals to orders-v2:8443.
Restoring orders-v1:8443 was followed by successful upstream connections and clearance of the 503 alert.

operation_logs.configuration_details: Reduced max_inflight_requests for the batch API worker pool from 240 to 60 to limit per-node memory use.
operation_logs.raw_evidence: Change record notes the prior value was 240 and the new value is 60.

operation_logs.configuration_details: Applied max_inflight_requests=60 to both batch API workers.
operation_logs.raw_evidence: Deployment status: complete on both workers; effective setting reported as 60.

operation_logs.configuration_details: Request concurrency reached the configured limit while incoming request volume was elevated.
operation_logs.incident_symptoms: Batch API p95 latency rose from 420 ms to 4.8 s, with requests accumulating in the worker queue.
operation_logs.raw_evidence: Worker logs on both nodes report inflight_requests=60 and queue_wait_ms above 3000. The request-rate monitor also recorded 1.9 times the usual volume during the same interval.

operation_logs.configuration_details: Restored max_inflight_requests to 240 on both workers.
operation_logs.incident_symptoms: Queue wait and p95 latency declined after the setting was restored, although request volume remained above usual levels.
operation_logs.raw_evidence: At 14:45Z, worker logs show queue_wait_ms below 500 while the request-rate monitor still reports elevated volume.

diagnosis_summary: The reduced concurrency limit constrained both workers during an elevated-traffic period, contributing to queue growth and high latency. Restoring the prior limit improved latency while request volume remained elevated, indicating the traffic surge was a cofactor rather than the sole explanation.
alternative_causes: Elevated request volume increased demand during the incident and likely contributed to queueing, but the improvement after restoring the concurrency limit shows it was not the only factor.

causal_evidence_chain.evidence_summary: The recorded change reduced the worker concurrency limit from 240 to 60.
The lower limit was deployed to both workers before the reported latency increase.
Both workers reached the new limit and accumulated queue wait while request volume was elevated; this supports a configuration contribution alongside increased demand.
Queue wait and latency declined after the prior limit was restored, even though request volume remained elevated.

diagnosis_summary: The database storage incident began 14 minutes before the audit-worker log-level change and remained confined to db-store-01. The change targeted a different asset and did not alter database storage settings, so the available logs do not support a causal link.

operation_logs.configuration_details: The database storage volume reached its capacity limit.
operation_logs.incident_symptoms: Database writes began failing with volume-capacity errors.
operation_logs.raw_evidence: Storage alert at 09:12Z: db-store-01 volume usage 100%; write failures recorded in the same minute.

operation_logs.configuration_details: Changed the audit worker log level from INFO to WARN on audit-worker-02.
operation_logs.raw_evidence: Change record identifies audit-worker-02 as the only target; no database storage settings were changed.

operation_logs.configuration_details: Applied the WARN log level to audit-worker-02.
Database write failures continued while the storage volume remained full.
operation_logs.incident_symptoms: Database writes continued to fail with volume-capacity errors.
operation_logs.raw_evidence: Alert history shows db-store-01 at 100% volume usage from 09:12Z through 09:34Z; the audit worker deployment targeted a different asset.

alternative_causes: The database volume reaching 100% capacity is directly recorded alongside the write failures and is the supported explanation for the incident.

causal_evidence_chain.evidence_summary: Database write failures and a full storage volume were recorded before the later configuration change.
The change affected only the audit worker's log level and did not modify database storage settings.
The change was deployed to audit-worker-02, not to the database asset reporting the incident.
The database remained at full volume with write failures; the logs identify no impact from the separate audit-worker deployment.
